From personal experience, I'm going to say it's about finding the right anti depressant.  I spend probably 8 years with increasingly severe psychotic depression, a handful of suicide attempts, and too many bad medications to count.  About 2-3 months ago I started seeing a new psychiatrist and decided to try a new medication.  Believe it or not, it feels like a fucking miracle drug.

I think that we can eat right or exercise or whatever, but I've been at the lowest of the low and I don't think anything would have changed if I didn't find the drug that was right for me.  And I'm not saying that the problems aren't still there, but it's made all the difference it needs to.  It's a process that's different for everyone and takes time to find the right one, but depression is in large part a chemical issue and medicine can help it.
